articles.title: There are five signs that someone dislikes you – but it’s best to ignore them | Polly Hudson
articles.summary: All the possible indications, from eye contact to body language, come with a disclaimer. The truth is, you can never be totally sure... I’d be far less paranoid if everyone wasn’t out to get me, so when BBC Science Focus dangled “ The subtle signs somebody secretly dislikes you ”, I’ve never…
body: The first indication? They avoid eye contact. Apparently “someone who repeatedly looks away, scans the room or avoids mutual gaze might be creating psychological distance”. Agreed. But they may also be checking to see who else arrives, which might not mean they secretly hate you, only that they secretly don’t like you as much as whoever just came in.

The second sign is unarguably more convincing. “Their facial expressions show contempt or disgust.” Admittedly, I’m no psychologist, but still, if someone looked contemptuous or disgusted while interacting with me, I’d be pretty confident in concluding that they aren’t my greatest fan all on my own. File this one under bear/woods, pope/Catholic.

Third up, they “smile less around you”. This feels dangerous, because the only way to know whether they are smiling less around you than other humans they come into contact with is to put them under surveillance and keep a tally. If they didn’t dislike you before you hid in a bush counting their grins, they probably would afterwards.

articles.title: The kindness of strangers: After my wife died, a football club made an extraordinary gesture
articles.summary: My son had only played two seasons for St Mary’s Greensborough, five years earlier. I don’t know how they even got our new address but they took the time to send him a care package. Footy clubs, and the AFL specifically, have a lot to answer for in terms of sexism.
body: When we lived in Melbourne many years ago, my son played a couple of seasons for St Mary’s Greensborough. Unfortunately for him, I secured a job in central Queensland and moved the family north.

During our new adventure, my wife was diagnosed with breast cancer. It was stage four, so she was in trouble straight away. She battled it fiercely but died in 2015, about five years after we left Melbourne.

As my children and I began to emerge from the fog of grief, a package arrived in the mail for my son. Inside was a St Mary’s Greensborough football jersey with our surname emblazoned across the back. Attached was a note that read: “Thinking of you after the loss of your mum.”
The support around us as a family when my wife was sick, and when she died, was fantastic. I am so grateful for that. But sometimes it’s the gestures that come out of left field that really move you.
points: My son had only played two seasons for St Mary’s Greensborough, five years earlier.
I don’t know how they even got our new address but they took the time to send him a care package.
Footy clubs, and the AFL specifically, have a lot to answer for in terms of sexism.

articles.title: Forget the seven-year itch: opposite-sex marriages more likely to end after two decades
articles.summary: ONS data for England and Wales shows 26% of heterosexual divorces in 2025 followed 20 years or more of marriage. Most couples are aware of the dreaded “seven-year itch”, when the honeymoon period wears off and real life starts to bite.
body: Now official data has shown that couples in England and Wales are more likely to split after 20 years. According to Office for National Statistics figures, more than a quarter of all divorces between opposite-sex couples happened after 20 years or longer of marriage.

The former Strictly presenter Tess Daly recently separated from her husband, the presenter Vernon Kay, after 22 years of marriage. The Downton Abbey actor Hugh Bonneville split from his wife, Lulu Williams, in 2023 after 25 years, and in 2019, Colin Firth announced his separation from wife, Livia Giuggioli, after 22. Last year, the Hollywood actor Nicole Kidman and singer Keith Urban separated after almost 20 years of marriage.

Divorce lawyers have previously said some couples are putting off splitting up because of the cost of living crisis. Recent figures have shown the average length of a marriage ending in divorce in England and Wales reached a record high last year.

ONS figures have long appeared to show that the seven-year itch exists; since records began in 1963, the largest proportion of divorces each year has almost always been among those who have spent between five and nine years as a couple.
points: ONS data for England and Wales shows 26% of heterosexual divorces in 2025 followed 20 years or more of marriage.

articles.title: The Most Evocative Period Dramas of the 21st Century
articles.summary: The best period dramas whisk viewers to times and places that feel a world away from modern life. Here are our favorites, from “Gosford Park” to “The Crown.”
body: Sumptuous costume dramas can provide a much-needed escape in troubling times, but if you’re tired of the usual assortment of airless parlors, manicured lawns, and straight-laced suitors, there is an alternative: a subset of recent films and series that play with our expectations of the genre. Combining post-punk soundtracks with cross-dressing, lobster racing, color-blind casting, and illicit love affairs, they allow us to view history through a new lens and feel surprisingly modern as a result. See our favorites below.

You can rely on Armando Iannucci to breathe new life into Charles Dickens’s sprawling bildungsroman. In the hands of the endlessly inventive comedian, the tale of a boy who pulls himself up by his bootstraps and seeks out fame and fortune becomes a madcap delight complete with a zingy script, cartoonish punch-ups, collapsing sets, and a heady dose of magical realism. Dev Patel is the dashing lead, supported by Peter Capaldi as a top-hatted menace and Tilda Swinton as an eccentric landowner who kicks trespassers off their donkeys.
points: The best period dramas whisk viewers to times and places that feel a world away from modern life.
Here are our favorites, from “Gosford Park” to “The Crown.”

articles.title: Stars Kept the Night Going at Giorgio Armani’s Academy Gala After-Party at Chateau Marmont
articles.summary: Right at the 10:30 p.m. kickoff, a flurry of camera flashes turned the sidewalk into a makeshift red carpet as paparazzi lined the street, eager to capture the industry’s brightest stars making their entrances.
body: With its storied charm, intimate atmosphere, and softly lit interiors, any night at Chateau Marmont is guaranteed to be a memorable one. Add a guest list overflowing with Hollywood crème de la crème to the mix and that magic is amplified tenfold. That was certainly true on Saturday night, when top-of-the-call-sheet names descended on the historic hotel for Giorgio Armani’s second annual Academy Museum Gala after-party.

Tracee Ellis Ross rolled in, nearly impossible to miss in her tangerine-hued, fringe-and-bead-adorned number from Balenciaga’s spring 2027 runway. She soon traded her barely-there, transparent high heels for white glove-style ballet flats in a practical fashion move. Others, however, tried to fly under the radar. Case in point: pals Leonardo DiCaprio and Tobey Maguire darted inside, heads down with their baseball caps pulled low.

The bash also doubled as a mini reunion for some. Shortly after arriving, Zoey Deutch caught the eye of Colman Domingo. “Zoey!” the actor exclaimed as he spotted her and pulled her close for a warm hug. Kate Hudson, who had swapped her earlier custom Armani Privé gown for a dramatic black feathered confection, soon joined the conversation.

articles.title: Chocolate Peanut Butter Gooey Cake
articles.summary: Put peanut butter in just about anything and I’m game, but swirl it into a three-layer fudgy chocolate bar and I’m actually powerless to resist. There’s something wonderfully nostalgic about the classic combination of chocolate and peanut butter.
body: For a gooey and decadent dessert, top boxed cake mix with a creamy peanut butter filling and chocolate-peanut butter ganache.

When I made this gooey cake, the peanut butter filling was the standout: creamy and decadent, with an almost cheesecake-like texture once baked. It sits between a fudgy devil’s food cake base and a glossy chocolate-peanut butter ganache, giving you three distinct layers between every bite. A little flaky salt on top cuts through the richness, provides a subtle crunch, and makes the classic chocolate-peanut butter pairing even harder to resist.

Heat the oven to 350℉. Coat a 9x13-inch metal baking pan with cooking spray. Line the bottom and two long sides with a sheet of parchment paper long enough to hang over the sides by a few inches to form a sling.

Stir 1 (15.25-ounce) box devil's food cake mix, 1 stick melted unsalted butter, and 1 large egg together in a large bowl until a thick dough forms. Transfer to the baking pan and press into an even layer with your hands or the bottom of a glass.

articles.title: Kendall Jenner Finally Got Her Polka-Dot Moment at the 2026 Academy Museum Gala
articles.summary: “I’ve always wanted a red carpet polka-dot moment," says Jenner of her custom Valentino gown. “It might be one of my favorites I’ve worn on a carpet.”
body: Last night, the 2026 Academy Museum Gala brought out Hollywood’s finest to the annual event, which supports the museum’s mission to preserve and celebrate cinema. Kim Kardashian! Taylor Swift! A$AP Rocky! The red carpet had no shortage of high-wattage star sightings, and also on hand was model Kendall Jenner (in custom Valentino, no less). “I love the Academy Gala. It’s so great we have this in L.A.,” Jenner tells Vogue the morning after. “Supporting the museum and film brings me such joy. To be in the room with such legends is an honor—but also to have friends and family there is so special! I truly enjoyed it all.”

This fall, Jenner has been keeping her head down with “a lot of work, and some play,” she says, so the Academy Gala was the perfect opportunity to step out and have some fun in a high-profile setting. “I’ve been great—feeling extremely blessed to have quite a healthy work-life balance,” says Jenner of what she’s been up to these past few months. “When I can, I’ve been hiding away and enjoying my animals and some quiet.”

articles.title: Retail Executives Speak Out After Store Looting in Paris
articles.summary: Protesters in Paris targeted luxury stores, including Burberry, Celine, and Lacoste, on Saturday.
body: “Today we have witnessed scenes of looting that have painfully targeted many clothing brands,” wrote Pierre-François Le Louët, co-president of Union Française des Industries Mode-Habillement (UFIMH) or French Union of Fashion and Clothing Industries, in a LinkedIn post.

calm had returned to the luxury shopping areas, with stores open again after closing late Saturday afternoon in response to the vandalism. Those that were looted remained closed, with boarded-up shopfronts, graffiti tags, and people busy making repairs inside. Graffiti tags read: “tax the rich”, “capitalism kills”, or “Fauchés mais en Lacoste”, which means “Broke but in Lacoste”.

articles.title: This Boxed Baking Mix Is So Good, I Pass It Off as My Own Recipe
articles.summary: I am a hardcore brownie-lover, and have been for decades. My brother, also famously a brownie-lover, and I would often fight over the middle of the pan for the rich, gooey center (I have since leaned into liking the edge pieces for the contrast of texture).
body: Bob’s Red Mill has been around since 1978, a cool 7 years before I was born, but I’ve only really discovered its products in the past 15 years or so. I use a lot of Bob’s Red Mill products in my day-to-day work as a cookbook author and recipe developer, and my fiancé, Theo, has a bowl of their Hot Buckwheat Cereal pretty much every day (sometimes a couple of bowls a day). But I’d admittedly slept on the baking mixes until I tested a bunch of gluten-free cake mixes over the summer.
I liked Bob’s cake mix so much that I decided to try more of the prepared mixes — and I’m so glad I did, because the blondies have made me something of a blondie convert.

Like any good boxed mix, the ingredients you’re asked to supply here are minimal and pretty typical staples: water, butter or oil, eggs, and vanilla. A peek at the ingredient list shows an equally minimal list of ingredients.

articles.title: “Gilmore Girls” Star Lauren Graham Shares the Famous Banana Muffin Recipe She Makes on Repeat
articles.summary: Lauren Graham is no stranger to the kitchen. Unlike her character Lorelai from the hit show Gilmore Girls, who relied mostly on coffee, takeout, candy, and diner grub at Luke’s, Lauren is actually a pretty good cook.
body: One of Lauren’s favorite fall activities is baking. (I can relate.) She recently partnered with baking essentials brand Bob’s Red Mill on its Moregetherness campaign to encourage people to use baking as a means to connect with each other.

“I thought: Oh, this is lovely. Moregetherness — more plus togetherness — is really about the way food can turn people who happen to live near one another into actual neighbors,” Lauren says. “People are lonely and disconnected, and I’m proud to work with a brand that wants to change that.” Bob’s Red Mill recently ran a campaign tied to National Good Neighbor Day on September 28 encouraging people to bake something and share it with a neighbor. “It’s a small gesture to tell people they matter. Sometimes that small gesture is all it takes to move from living near someone to actually knowing them,” Lauren says.

In the spirit of bringing people together over baked goods, I got a chance to chat with Lauren about her favorite things to make this fall, how she takes her coffee, and more. Here’s our conversation.

articles.title: This Is One of the Best Bedroom Splurges, According to a Top Home Stager
articles.summary: If you’re itching for a primary bedroom makeover, there’s a professional home stager-approved item that’s a total game changer and worth the investment. Not only will it bring you comfort, but it can also dramatically change the vibe of your bedroom and could be a long-lasting purchase.
body: What is it, you ask? In the second episode of Apartment Therapy’s Styled to Sell series, professional stager Jason Saft says the best purchase you can make for your primary bedroom is a high-quality, good-looking rug.

A high-quality rug, while usually on the pricier side, is a great investment because often they’re made of wool (which means they’re durable). Bedrooms aren’t necessarily high-traffic areas, so you don’t have to worry too much about the rug getting damaged like you would in a communal area.

While the first step is simply beginning your rug search, along the way you’ll want to make sure you’re picking something that’s the right size for anchoring the bed. If you have a king-size bed, it’s best to choose a large, 9’x12′ rug to make sure that your bed is actually surrounded by that plushness. That said, a rug doesn’t necessarily have to go directly underneath the bed. If budget doesn’t allow for a big rug, opt for a smaller one and put it on one side of the bed.
